{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment ≤ 0.25) and model shows overconfidence (high forecast peaks).",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast deviates > ±10% from recent 5-day average, reduce or increase forecast by 50% of the deviation.",
    "Reduce forecast overshoot after sharp spikes: if true outcome drops > 5% from peak, cap forecast decline at 30% of peak deviation.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices: if last 3 days show falling prices, adjust forecast downward by 2–5% per day.",
    "For sentiment > 0.5, increase forecast volatility by 10% to reflect bullish momentum, but cap at 15% above historical range.",
    "If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast (e.g., 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast by 5% per day to avoid overestimation.",
    "When sentiment is 0.00 and forecast is > 65.00, apply downward bias of 3–5% to reflect market cooling.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, apply exponential decay weighting: recent 7-day data dominates 70% of adjustment."
  ]
}
